subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a delegate-only/self-deny tool policy for requester agents, and what public config/API shape should own that inherited-tool security boundary?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix would add public config surface and allow tools hidden from the requester to remain available to children, which automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Sponsor delegate-only config
options.body: Add a documented `selfDeny` or `delegateOnly`-style field with absolute deny precedence, effective-tool visibility, inherited-policy tests, docs, and ACP/runtime behavior explicitly defined.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy design
options.body: Keep this open until the per-spawn tool restriction design also covers requester-hidden but child-inherited tools under one policy model.

options.title: Reject new core surface
options.body: Document separate agent IDs or prompt-level delegation as the supported pattern and accept that config-enforced separation of duties remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Sponsor delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add a documented `selfDeny` or `delegateOnly`-style field with absolute deny precedence, effective-tool visibility, inherited-policy tests, docs, and ACP/runtime behavior explicitly defined.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent path-history and prior-review signal for the cross-cutting tool-policy, docs, and security/API decision.
